newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Left seeking to probe CVRD selloff.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Left seeking to probe CVRD selloff.

text.p: A left-wing political party, opposed to the privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, is seeking to set up a parlimentary inquiry into what it says are irregularities in the upcoming selloff of the company, an official said.

The Worker's Party (PT) on Wednesday began collecting signatures for a petition which could lead to the creation of a Parlimentary Committee of Inquiry (CPI) into the CVRD privatization, PT spokesman Itamar Garcez said.
"If we manage to hold a CPI there won't be the right kind of climate for privatizing CVRD. Of course we face an uphill struggle," Garcez said.
The PT needs the support of one third of Brazil's senators and deputies for the CPI to be set up.
Left-wing parties have sought without success on several occasions to block the CVRD privatization through legislation that would have made the sale subject to congressional approval.

Garcez said the CPI, if created, would look into allegations by another left-wing party that U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch failed to declare an alleged conflict of interest when it was appointed to advise the Brazilian government on the CVRD selloff.

Last week the Democratic Labour Party (PDT) claimed that Merrill Lynch's ownership of a South African brokerage, which is a client of mining conglomerate Anglo-American, a potential bidder for CVRD, represented a conflict of interest.

Merrill Lynch has denied the allegations. The PT also wants to investigate claims the CVRD sale price is undervalued. The Brazilian government is due to auction on April 29 40-45 percent of the voting shares of CVRD, in the first stage of the company's privatization.
